title: Elytra Energy - Inference Security Onboarding Call
summary: Initial security posture discovery for Elytra Energy evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Main concerns: SOC2 and ISO alignment, SSO/SAML and RBAC, KMS integration and key isolation, audit logs/retention, and data residency for EU projects. Agreed to exchange SOC2 report, network diagrams, and follow-up benchmark for POC (latency & cost).
next_steps: Avery to send SOC2 + ISO summary and latest pen test report by 2026-09-07
Priya to share Elytra network diagram and list of required IP ranges by 2026-09-09
Samir to propose a POC test plan (throughput/latency) and a cost estimate for Dedicated by 2026-09-10
Schedule follow-up technical deep-dive with Elytra infra team week of 2026-09-14
action_items: Avery Chen - Email SOC2 report and security deck - due 2026-09-07
Priya Kumar - Share VPC diagram and compliance checklist - due 2026-09-09
Samir Patel - Draft POC perf plan and required infra for Dedicated/Private - due 2026-09-10
header:
Date: 2026-09-04
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Monica Reyes (Elytra CISO), Liam O'Neal (Head of ML), Priya Kumar (Cloud Architect), Jason Mills (DevOps)
Meeting recorded
transcript:
00:00 Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account. Samir and I will run through security intake - quick intro then dig into your constraints.
00:14 Monica Reyes: Hi, Monica here. We're mostly trying to understand how Redwood would fit into our regulated workloads. We've got projects in EU and NA, so residency and keys matter.
00:30 Samir Patel: Great — quick high level: Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and a private deployment option (VPC or on-prem). We'll map those to your compliance and latency needs.
00:45 Liam O'Neal: For the ML team, latency and cost per token both matter. But Monica's team mandates certain crypto and audit guarantees.
00:58 Priya Kumar: Also we need SSO via SAML to integrate with our IdP, and we require RBAC that mirrors our org structure.
01:12 Jason Mills: And IP allowlists — we can't open up wide egress, so need to know IP ranges for dedicated and hosted.
01:30 Avery Chen: Totally. Quick Qs to frame - are you currently SOC2 or ISO27001 certified? And do you have a preferred key management approach (customer-managed KMS vs vendor-managed)?
01:44 Monica Reyes: We're SOC2 Type II in scope, working on ISO27001; we prefer customer-managed keys where possible for core PII/workflows.
01:57 Samir Patel: Makes sense. For Redwood Private you can bring your own KMS or HSM; for Dedicated we support KMS integration (customer-owned keys in cloud KMS) and have an option for envelope encryption for hosted.
02:15 Liam O'Neal: When you say envelope, do you mean we still send plaintext to Redwood? Need to be explicit for legal.
02:26 Samir Patel: Short answer: for hosted API the service has access to decrypted content to run inference, but with envelope keys you control the master key. For Private, you can keep everything within your VPC where we don't have key access.
02:45 Monica Reyes: So Private is the only true zero-access model?
02:50 Samir Patel: Correct, Private/on-prem can be configured so Redwood control plane is separate and customer keys never leave their KMS.
03:05 Monica: Ok. Audit logs — we need immutable audit trails across model calls and admin actions, 7 years retention for some projects. Is that realistic?
03:20 Avery: We capture request metadata, token counts, user IDs, and admin actions in our audit store. Retention tunable — 90 days default in hosted, but Dedicated/Private can extend with log export to your S3 or SIEM. Seven years is operationally heavy but doable for Private with archival.
03:40 Priya: Export formats? SIEM friendly?
03:44 Samir: Yes, logs stream via syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver or you can ship to S3 with lifecycle. They include route, model version, request ID, token usage, and user context. Note: some customers later redacted user prompts before long-term storage.
04:05 Monica: Are there any certifications or third-party audits we can exchange?
04:10 Avery: We'll send our SOC2 Type II report excerpts and an ISO readiness summary. Also our pen-test summary. Full reports require an NDA, but standard practice.
04:22 Jason: Network connectivity — if we pick Dedicated in GCP, what IPs do we need to allow?
04:30 Samir: We'll provide region-specific egress ranges. For Dedicated we usually have static egress nodes; for hosted public API it's a larger ephemeral range. We'll ask Priya for preferred region.
04:42 Priya: EU-west for our EU workloads. Also need data residency constraints per project.
04:50 Avery: Understood. We'll map routing policies — you can pin certain projects to EU-only serving nodes.
05:05 Liam: How do you handle model rollouts and rollback? Our concern is regression causing PII leaks or hallucination spikes.
05:20 Samir: Canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback to previous model version on anomaly detection. We can tie quality monitors to prompt sets and trigger alerts or auto-revert.
05:40 Monica: Can you show where RBAC shows up? Our security team wants separation between admin (billing, rollout) and ML devs who can call models but not change keys.
05:52 Samir: RBAC is per-route and per-model; we integrate with SAML groups and map to roles. Admin console has audit trail for role changes. We'll share the RBAC matrix and sample policies.
06:10 Priya: About SSO — do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning? We need automated user lifecycle.
06:18 Avery: Yes SAML2.0 and SCIM are supported for both Hosted and Dedicated control planes. For Private deployments you can run the control plane behind your IdP.
06:32 Monica: Encryption at rest — does Redwood encrypt disk-level and object storage by default?
06:38 Samir: Yes, everything encrypted at rest. For Hosted we manage keys — but with envelope encryption you supply the master key in your KMS. For Dedicated you can bring KMS keys.
06:52 Liam: Any limitations on model quantization or kernel selection that impact determinism/logging?
06:59 Samir: Good question. Quantization changes tokenization timing but not logs. Determinism is influenced by sampling settings. Kernel choices are internal optimizations; we log model variant and kernel id in the trace for reproducibility.
07:20 Monica: Data retention again — can we configure prompt retention to auto-delete after X days and persist embeddings longer? We have to redact PII in prompts but embed features are allowed to be retained.
07:34 Avery: Yes, retention policies can be separate for raw requests vs derived artifacts like embeddings. Many customers choose short prompt retention and long embedding retention with access controls.
07:50 Priya: Regarding legal/procurement, will Redwood sign standard DPA and security addenda?
07:56 Avery: Yes, we have templated DPA and security addenda, and can negotiate enterprise terms for Dedicated/Private contracts.
08:08 Jason: For POCs, we want to run a benchmark: 1k concurrent calls, mix of short and long sequences, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies. Can Redwood set that up in Dedicated?
08:22 Samir: Absolutely; Samir: we can provision a short-lived Dedicated pool or Private sandbox for POC benchmarking. We'll need expected sequences and dataset. We'll also provide cost projections.
08:38 Liam: On the topic of audit logs again — do logs include prompt text by default? If so, can we mask sensitive fields before sent to logs?
08:46 Samir: By default request payload is logged, but you can opt out or set masking rules. For compliance we usually suggest client-side redaction for the highest assurance.
08:58 Priya: Will need details on masking API and SDK hooks.
09:04 Avery: We'll include sample SDK snippet and config for masking.
09:12 Monica: Any MDR/SIEM integration? We have Splunk and Sumo.
09:16 Samir: Splunk/Sumo/Datadog integrations available; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. We can also push alerts to PagerDuty on anomalies.
09:28 Monica: About incident response — do you publish SLAs and incident timelines?
09:33 Avery: SLA docs are in the enterprise pack for Dedicated. For Private we can align response SLAs in the contract. We'll share a summary.
09:44 Liam: Encryption key rotation — how often and who controls rotation?
09:48 Samir: If you use your KMS, you control rotation schedule. For vendor-managed keys we rotate per our policy and share logs of rotations.
10:02 Priya: Curious about access: does Redwood staff ever get admin console access for debugging?
10:08 Avery: Access is limited and audited. For support we do time-bounded, logged sessions that require customer approval for Private. For Hosted we have runbooks and sanitized telemetry; privileged access is tightly controlled.
10:30 Jason: We need to define the list of allowed support actions and escalation matrix.
10:36 Avery: We'll include our support playbook excerpt.
10:42 Speaker 6: (inaudible) question about data residency in backups — are snapshots replicated outside region?
10:49 Samir: Snapshots stay in-region unless you explicitly enable cross-region replication — we'll default to region-local for EU.
11:05 Monica: Great. Can you send over sample contract language for data residency and key custody?
11:12 Avery: Yes, we'll include standard clauses and a draft SOW for Dedicated/Private options.
11:24 Priya: For timeline — we're aiming to pick a vendor by end of Q4, but initial POC in October.
11:34 Avery: Sounds good. We'll target that. Samir: I'll draft the POC checklist.
11:45 Monica: One last question — does Redwood provide attestation for non-production environments? We keep dev data in a separate bucket with more permissive retention.
11:52 Samir: We can provide attestation and segmentation between prod and non-prod, and sandbox environments with different retention.
12:03 Avery: Thanks everyone. Recap and next steps: we'll email SOC2 pack + pen test, Samir will send POC plan, Priya to share VPC diagram. Schedule next technical deep dive week of 9/14.
12:18 Monica: Thanks all.
12:22 Meeting ends.
